report.verdict: Cobalt Pay asks for an engineering manager; your resume shows senior backend work, not people management.
write_up: The Cobalt Pay role is an engineering management job, while your resume points to senior backend engineering. Your payments work is strong: you show how you built a high-volume payouts service, moved the ledger and improved the balance API.

The balance API line is a great model because it connects a technical change to a before-and-after result. Your experience leads your education, and your progression from insurance to freight to payments is easy to follow.

For a senior backend role, your resume is unlikely to be what stands between you and a callback. For Cobalt Pay, bring the incident review work forward and add any formal management responsibilities you can substantiate. The competitiveness of the role and a referral can matter too.

cards.where: Senior Software Engineer, Payments Platform, line 3
cards.line: Cut p99 latency on the balance API from 900 ms to 140 ms by moving reads to a Kafka-fed cache
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It names the service, the change you made and the measure on both sides, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess what improved.

cards.where: Senior Software Engineer, Payments Platform, line 5
cards.line: Mentor two mid-level engineers through code review and design docs
cards.cannot_tell: For a manager role, formal responsibility for people or team direction would build on this mentoring work if you've had it.
cards.example: Mentor two mid-level engineers through code review and design docs and [formal management responsibility]
cards.question: Have you had formal management responsibilities in this role, and what were they?

fit.why: Your headline and current role center on backend payments services, ledger migration and production operations.
fit.level: senior, leads a ledger migration and mentors two engineers
fit.note: Your payouts and ledger work fits Cobalt Pay's platform. Move the incident review line higher in the current role so that work is easy to find.
